ledger.x: c. 844: the earliest recorded Chera Perumal reigns begin at Mahodayapuram. Infobox "c. 844 CE-c. 1124 CE" with spans "c. 844-870 (earliest recorded)", "c. 905-943", "962-1021" and "c. 1089-1124 (last)". The page names no founder.
11th century (bridge 1001): northern Kerala comes under Chera influence.
11th century (bridge 1001): the kingdom is said to have "later extended up to the Chandragiri river in northern Kerala and to Nagercoil in the south".
ledger.cp: unknown (page silent on who held it)

ledger.x: c. 1097: Chola forces reach Kollam. They "advanced northwards from the south (Nagercoil) as far as the port of Kollam around 1097 AD", "probably led by" the general Kalinga Rayan. Earlier, "Between 1077 and 1081 AD, the Chola ruler Kulottunga I (1070-1120) conducted a campaign."
c. 1124: the kingdom breaks up. "In the early 12th century, the medieval Chera kingdom of Kerala dissolved into several local powers"; Kolathunadu goes with the north.

c. 1124: the Chera Perumal kingdom dissolves. Infobox end c. 1124; a 1126 Cholapuram inscription calls Vira Kerala "the first independent ruler of Venadu". Venad, Kolathunadu and the future rulers of Kozhikode and Kochi are the successors; the last Perumal "disappeared from the Kerala 'mysteriously'" after dividing…

wars.name: Chola subjugation of the Chera Perumals
wars.outcome: "The Chera kingdom was attacked and eventually forced into submission by the Cholas in c. early 11th century CE"; "The Chera state in Kerala was subjugated during the reign of the Chola emperor Rajaraja I" (died 1014 per the Rajaraja I page) and Chola…

wars.name: Chola campaign to Kollam
wars.outcome: Chola forces advanced from Nagercoil to Kollam around 1097; by 1102 Rama Kulasekhara "appears to have recovered Kollam".

certainty.note: No frontier is given on any page; the Palakkad Gap and Vembanad Lake mark the core, the rest is approximate.
